about: One mesh bound to a skeleton: two buffers of skinning matrices (3x4 floats a mesh bone, inverse bind times world, in the entity's space), rewritten every frame while the entity is animated, and the skeleton bone each mesh bone follows.

evidence.says: adding 0.6 to the translation of every matrix after the Effect system's update draws the figure 0.6 m higher; each matrix equals the bone's inverse bind matrix times its world matrix for the bone the array at 0xA0 names

The field's place and name come from the struct our build of Script Extender declares for this type; no read or watch of the field itself backs it.
each skinning matrix equals the inverse bind matrix times the world matrix of the skeleton bone this array names for it

adding 0.6 to the translation of every matrix after the Effect system's update draws the figure 0.6 m higher; each matrix equals the bone's inverse bind matrix times its world matrix for the bone the array at 0xA0 names

The name is ours: it is the name of the struct our build of Script Extender declares, set in the namespace of code:gr::GrannySkeleton, which holds the bindings. No store holds gr::MeshBinding: the macOS build's symbols have none, and the Toolkit's GameEngine.dll exports a class ls::MeshBinding (a constructor, an assignment, GetBound, GetAnimationBound) that was not compared with this layout.

questions.ask: Whether this is the game's ls::MeshBinding: read the constructor GameEngine.dll exports and compare what it writes with the fields here; the id follows the answer.
Which of the two poses is the current frame's and which the previous one's: write one alone and look at motion blur.
